page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.18xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8559C x86_64 processor offering 36 physical cores and 72 dedicated vCPUs operating at a nominal clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The compute architecture features a large 320 MB L3 cache alongside support for instruction extensions including AVX-512 and AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for matrix math acceleration. Memory capacity totals 576.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 running at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Storage and network resources are scaled for severe I/O demands. The instance bundles 45,000 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage directly attached, bypassing network storage bottlenecks. External throughput is backed by a 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no discrete graphics hardware, directing all host power and memory toward storage processing, compute threads, and throughput-intensive network activity.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate top-tier execution across high-concurrency tasks. In Geekbench testing, the server achieved a multi-core score of 20,730.0 and a single-core score of 2,297.0, placing both in the top 10% of tested instances. Multi-core stress-ng performance reached 69,824.62, while static web serving throughput reached 109.44 GB/sec. Memory subsystem bandwidth measured 287.15 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 120.7 GB/sec for writes. PassMark database tests recorded 32,734.62 operations, paired with Redis throughput achieving 91.92 million SET operations per second.

Because the server combines massive local NVMe capacity, 576 GB of DDR5 memory, and high network bandwidth, it yields high operational efficiency for large-scale caching, data lakes, distributed file systems, high-volume transactional databases, and real-time search clusters that rely on fast I/O rather than GPU acceleration.
